issues.legal_issue: Deductions from the price of a small developed exemplar sale may be made when valuing a large undeveloped acquired tract, provided the deductions reflect the differences between the lands and remain within the applicable overall limits.
material_facts: The acquired land was a large tract of undeveloped agricultural land without independent irrigation facilities and surrounded by similar land.
The exemplar transaction concerned a small, fully developed site.
The courts assessed a development deduction by comparing the condition of the acquired land with the developed exemplar.
The landowners did not establish the development expenditure for the entire acquired area; the authority had declined to provide expenditure information for the particular parcel.
The High Court applied deductions of 55 percent for development, 10 percent for de-escalation and 5 percent for waiting period, totalling 70 percent.
issues.conclusion: The development deduction of 55 percent and the cumulative deductions of 70 percent were within the permissible limits and were upheld. Development deductions may be assessed by comparing the lands even when actual expenditure on the particular acquired parcel is not shown.
issues.legal_principle: Development deductions have two components: land or space set aside for infrastructure and civic amenities, and expenditure on providing that infrastructure and amenities. The facts of each case determine the appropriate deduction for each component, but deductions under development should not exceed 67 percent. Other deductions may also be made on the facts, but all deductions together should not exceed 75 percent; a sale requiring a greater total deduction is not a relevant comparable. The comparison should classify the exemplar and acquired lands by their respective levels of development. Actual expenditure on a particular parcel is not decisive because development costs are assessed for the acquired area as a whole and may be apportioned among landholders. These principles draw on Brigadier Sahib Singh Kalha v. Amritsar Improvement Trust, Administrator General of West Bengal v. Collector, Varanasi, Chimanlal Hargovinddas v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Land Acquisition Officer v. L. Kamalamma, Kasturi v. State of Haryana, Land Acquisition Officer v. Nookala Rajamallu, V. Hanumantha Reddy v. Land Acquisition Officer, Viluben Jhalejar Contractor v. State of Gujarat, Atma Singh v. State of Haryana, Lal Chand v. Union of India, Subh Ram v. State of Haryana, Andhra Pradesh Housing Board v. K. Manohar Reddy, and Special Land Acquisition Officer v. M.K. Rafiq Sahib.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_case and large_undeveloped_acquired_land and small_developed_exemplar and deductions_assessed_by_comparing_development and cumulative_deductions_within_overall_limit

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns compensation for land acquired by a public authority.
predicates.large_undeveloped_acquired_land: A large tract of acquired land was undeveloped or less developed than the land used for comparison.
predicates.small_developed_exemplar: The valuation relied on a sale of a small developed parcel.
predicates.deductions_assessed_by_comparing_develop: The court assessed deductions by comparing the development of the acquired land with that of the exemplar land.
predicates.cumulative_deductions_within_overall_lim: The development and other deductions together did not exceed the applicable overall limit.

issues.definition: When a compensation case involves a large, less-developed acquired tract valued by reference to a small developed parcel, deductions assessed by comparing their development are upheld if the cumulative deductions remain within the overall limit.

issues.legal_issue: A deduction may be made to account for the time difference when the exemplar sale occurred after the relevant acquisition notification and land prices were rising.
material_facts: The exemplar sale occurred one year and more than seven months after publication of the preliminary acquisition notification.
The High Court deducted 10 percent for de-escalation in valuing the acquired land.
Earlier decisions had approved annual escalation rates ranging from 7.5 percent to 10 percent, and the Court took notice of the general rise in land prices.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's 10 percent deduction for de-escalation was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Although escalation in land prices is ordinarily a question of fact to be proved by cogent evidence, the Court may take judicial notice of rising land prices in light of ground realities. The decisions in Delhi Development Authority v. Bali Ram Sharma, ONGC Ltd. v. Rameshbhai Jeewanbhai Patel, and Valliyammal v. Special Tehsildar support annual escalation rates within the range of 7.5 to 10 percent. A time-based adjustment was justified where the exemplar sale occurred more than a year after the preliminary notification.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_case and exemplar_sale_after_notification and sale_more_than_a_year_later and rising_land_prices

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns compensation for land acquired by a public authority.
predicates.exemplar_sale_after_notification: The exemplar transaction took place after publication of the preliminary acquisition notification.
predicates.sale_more_than_a_year_later: More than a year elapsed between publication of the notification and the exemplar transaction.
predicates.rising_land_prices: The court found that land prices were generally rising during the relevant period.

issues.definition: A time-difference deduction is upheld in a compensation case when the exemplar sale occurred more than a year after the notification and land prices were rising.

issues.legal_issue: A deduction for the waiting period involved in developing and selling land may be upheld when that period is relevant to valuing acquired land from a developed exemplar.
material_facts: The High Court deducted 5 percent for the waiting period involved in development and sale.
The landowners did not challenge that deduction before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The 5 percent waiting-period deduction was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Waiting time is a relevant factor in adjusting the value of a developed exemplar when determining compensation for acquired land. The Court relied on Chimanlal Hargovinddas v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Land Acquisition Officer v. L. Kamalamma, and Atma Singh v. State of Haryana.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns compensation for land acquired by a public authority.
predicates.waiting_period_relevant_to_valuation: A period required for development or sale of the land was relevant to determining its value from the exemplar.
predicates.landowners_do_not_challenge_waiting_peri: The landowners did not contest the lower court's deduction for the waiting period.

issues.definition: A waiting-period deduction is upheld when it is relevant to the valuation and the landowners do not challenge it.

issues.legal_issue: Consistency in valuation supports maintaining a final compensation determination for comparable land acquired through the same acquisition process.
material_facts: The High Court had previously fixed compensation for land acquired in the same acquisition process at the same rate ultimately awarded to the appellants.
The earlier determination had attained finality, and the land in the earlier proceeding had not been shown to differ from the land in question.
The connected appeals concerned land from another revenue estate that the High Court regarded as having a lower market value because it was farther from the town centre.
The Supreme Court nevertheless considered the same compensation rate appropriate for the connected land in the circumstances of the case.
issues.conclusion: The compensation fixed by the High Court was affirmed for both sets of appeals, including the connected land considered to have a lower market value.
issues.legal_principle: Consistency in judicial determination is important. Where land acquired through the same process has been assigned a final value in an earlier proceeding and the land is not shown to be materially different, maintaining a uniform valuation is justified. The Court also affirmed the value for the connected land in the particular circumstances before it.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and land_acquired_in_same_process and prior_compensation_determination_is_final and court_finds_uniform_valuation_appropriate

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.land_acquired_in_same_process: The land was acquired through the same acquisition process as land addressed in another compensation determination.
predicates.prior_compensation_determination_is_fina: An earlier compensation determination concerning land acquired through that process has become final.
predicates.court_finds_uniform_valuation_appropriat: The court considered a uniform valuation appropriate in the circumstances, including any relevant differences between the lands.

issues.definition: A compensation determination is maintained consistently when land was acquired through the same process, an earlier determination is final, and the court considers uniform valuation appropriate.
